# Doug Hindson

## Creative Director Art Director Designer etc.

Oslo, Norway

(+47) 412 66 789
[hello@doughindson.com](mailto:hello@doughindson.com)

Find me on [Vimeo](http://www.vimeo.com/doughindson) & [Instagram](http://www.instagram.com/doughindson).

*All work © Doug Hindson unless otherwise stated.*

My aim is to bring a thoughtful approach to whatever it is that I tackle; creativity with a strong sense of design and an emphasis on concept and storytelling. Whether that be through design, animation, illustration, photography or carving a spoon from a slab of oak.

Currently leading the design department at [NewsLab](https://www.newslab.no/) in Oslo, across a wide range of design, illustration and motion projects.

Before that I was an Associate Creative Director at [Buck](https://buck.co) in NYC for four and a half years, and spent five years in London, where I had the pleasure of working with companies such as [Studio AKA](https://www.studioaka.co.uk), [Chromosphere LA](http://chromosphere-la.com), [Nexus Studios](https://nexusstudios.com), and [Google Creative Lab](http://www.creativelab5.com/) among others.

My work has been shown at festivals across the world and I'm the proud owner of a [D&AD Award](https://www.dandad.org/awards/new-blood/2014/dcm-show-the-emotion-of-film/2433/frisson/), [Vimeo Staff Pick](https://vimeo.com/116533375) and was a finalist for the [ADC Young Guns](https://www.shootonline.com/news/lineup-global-finalists-set-one-clubs-young-guns-19).

Graduated with First Class Honours in Illustration & Animation BA(Hons) at Kingston University 2014.

# DIS \ CONNECT

Some of the most powerful and emotional moments in cinema have also been the most tense, the most thrilling. This film aims to capture that moment of 'frisson' - a sudden strong feeling of excitement or fear; a thrill.

‘DIS \ CONNECT’ was my graduation film from the Illustration & Animation course at Kingston University. All models and sets were hand-made from wood & card, hundreds of individual pieces were designed, cut, sanded, glued and painted. Rather than stop-motion, the film was shot live-action with strings and rods controlling the puppets and everything was captured in-camera.

# Google - Project Bloks

### Role: **Animation Direction** Client: **Google** Studio: **Google Creative Lab**

## Creating a development platform for tangible programming.

Google Creative Lab created a modular system for tangible programming made up of electronic boards and programmable pucks — which enable you to send instructions to devices when connected together. Our aim is to create an open hardware platform to help developers, designers, and researchers build the next generation of tangible programming experiences for kids.

We wanted the film to reflect the nature of the coding kits; tactile, dynamic and life-size. This meant using the real circuit boards and developing an animation style that could work alongside them and feel real whilst still alluding to the fact that the coding kits were examples rather than finished products.

Paper craft and stop-motion was the perfect fit, it allowed us the flexibility to create models that had texture and also show hands interacting with them.

I was tasked with developing the motion design principles and directing the animation. This involved working on the initial look and feel for the treatment, full storyboarding & animatics, and planning the in-camera animation techniques. I was then directing animation on set and working alongside our production team.

We developed the film internally at Google Creative Lab, working with the incredible designers & animators [Nearly Normal](http://www.nearlynormal.tv) and production company F1lm Club.

[See the full project site.](https://projectbloks.withgoogle.com)

Transportation Alternatives — Doug Hindson — Creative Director

blocks.markdown: # Transportation Alternatives

*Role:*  Associate Creative Director, Design

*Studio:*  BUCK

*Client:*  Transportation Alternatives

To accompany the release of Transportation Alternative’s new Spatial Equity NYC tool, Buck created a short film that highlights how data can reveal the inequities across NYC streets and city planning — and provide positive solutions for the people of New York.

Some streets are wide and leafy, others narrow and steamy, and the rest are famously congested. One size does not fit all in New York’s terra firma.

Those differences, though, can create inequitable consequences for its citizens, and Transportation Alternatives have been working with MIT on a tool that aims to reveal those disparities.

The tool, Spatial Equity NYC, uses publicly-available data to measure, compare, and visualise different types of public space—from streets to bus lanes to parks—between neighbourhoods.

That data is then paired with demographic data, from street-level to city wide. The hope is that the tool will be utilised by New Yorkers from all walks of life to improve the streets and make the city safer and fairer for everyone.

We separated our story into four different threads following characters and the common problems they face in the city. After establishing each scenario, we then see problems become solutions, all brought together by our loose visual interpretation of the data.

The film uses dramatic lighting to help communicate its themes. There’s a dark, foreboding feeling to the setup of the city’s spatial problems, but as the film provides ideas and solutions, the lighting brightens, full of optimism and hope.

pages.title: Citibank — Illustrations — Doug Hindson — Creative Director

blocks.markdown: # Citibank — Illustrations

*Role:*  Art Director

*Studio:*  BUCK

*Client* : Turner Duckworth / Citibank

Two sets of illustrations built for the Citi brand, meant to speak to two of their most important groups of clients — institutions and everyday banking customers.

Institutional clients include some of the biggest companies in the world, so this first set of illustrations had to speak to the issues and scenarios that these businesses consider each day — from cultural differences across world markets, to the future of energy and transportation.

This set of illustrations were intentionally restrained; making minimal use of light and shadow to bring dimensionality without overdoing it.

The consumer illustrations needed to cover more down to earth activities — from the weekly groceries to a new home mortgage. We embraced exaggeration, amplifying parts of the design in order to add energy to a moment, draw attention to the message, or emphasize motion & action.

People and objects are rooted in fairly realistic anatomy and proportions, with exaggeration applied to emphasize mood, action, or pull focus. With nuanced facial expressions and dynamic body language, all allowing personal style to come to the fore.

The final component was a set of dynamic, abstract 3D background elements, inspired by the arc in the Citi logo. Materials and textures were used that exude luxury and opulence (such as silk or satin), all in service of making these forms feel tangible, familiar, and high-end.

Lighting was used to bring depth and dimension to the shape; highlights picking out edges of folds, shadows pushing things back in space.

The motion of the abstract 3D sculpture brings the dynamic form to life. Evoking a sense of evolution, movement, tension and release.

pages.title: IBM — Illustrations — Doug Hindson — Creative Director

blocks.markdown: # IBM — Illustrations

*Role:*  Associate Creative Director, Art Director, Designer

*Studio:*  BUCK

*Client:*  IBM

IBM has developed a rigorous design system over the decades, with a thorough consideration for every detail covering a broad range of different brand expressions.

BUCK built out a varied set of illustrations, meant to show the full breadth of visual concepts that might need to be represented, while staying within the constraints of the IBM design language.

The IBM design system is anchored around a grid system, so each shape needs to carefully adhere to regular increments of scale and spacing. Respecting a visual hierarchy and allowing for usage across a wide range of placements.
Each illustration tackled a broad theme — from practical concepts like ‘security’ and ‘cloud computing’, to more amorphous ideas like 'problem solving’.
Alongside the broader set of conceptual illustrations, we were also tasked with developing a robust array of icons that would cover specific topics whilst working across many different applications.
These icons were rooted in the isometric IBM design language, and had to be able to be able to be scaled across many sizes, and work against both light and dark environments.

pages.title: Thorne — Healthy Aging — Doug Hindson — Creative Director

blocks.markdown: # Thorne — Healthy Aging

*Role:*  Art Director

*Studio:*  BUCK

*Client:*  Thorne

Through a novel combination of painting, live-action, and 3D, BUCK told told a poetic story about healthy aging for Thorne.

Steering away from traditional supplement commercials’ obsession with “anti-aging,” we focused instead on an aspirational view of healthy aging that delivers a holistic lifestyle, rather than a cure.

Playing with scale and surrealism, we created a set of sublime environments for real people to inhabit as we told our story.

The paintings themselves set the tone for each of the scenes, meaning the 3D elements needed to feel integrated and embedded with each landscape.

Matching lighting between the painted world and our 3D objects helped to unify each environment. As well as modeling the products, we also used 3D to bring depth to landscape elements in scenes with dynamic cameras, adding parallax and a sense of depth where it was needed.
Our starting point was loose painting exploration —playing with ways to integrate humans and objects in natural landscapes in a way that pushed scale, lighting and saturation.
We took inspiration from Surrealist masters like Magritte & Dali, as well as Romanticists like Caspar David Friedrich, where landscapes tell as much of a story as the people and objects within them.
Creating a mood film of footage of the natural world showed us locations for exploration and started to give us a sense of pacing and camera movement.
We also used some cutting edge machine learning (EBSynth) to apply our painted style to some complex elements, like clouds and water.

pages.title: Microsoft — 365 — Doug Hindson — Creative Director

blocks.markdown: # Microsoft — 365

*Role:*  Art Director

*Studio:*  BUCK

*Client:*  Microsoft

Microsoft’s full suite of productivity software has always been well known, but in an era of increasingly remote teams, collaboration was a more important aspect than ever.

Our team at BUCK brought all of these collaborative features to life in a way that combined dimensional product UI with a playful mixed media approach. Showing each tool being used in a whole myriad of ways.

A broad suite of tools called for a broad range of stylistic approaches. We used a combination of hand-drawn 2D design & animation, along with textural 3D scenes, to create varied representations of each of the key features we were highlighting.

These were combined with richly tactile user interface elements, lifting off the screen. This allowed us to bring further focus and emphasis to key elements, while still keeping one foot grounded in the realism of the software itself.

pages.title: IBM — watsonx — Doug Hindson — Creative Director

blocks.markdown: # IBM — watsonx

*Role:*  Art Director

*Studio:*  BUCK

*Client:*  IBM

Building on the Watson name and its established reputation for advancing AI, BUCK worked closely with IBM’s Blue Studio to reimagine *watsonx*  as the new face of AI within IBM’s impressive enterprise solutions.

BUCK built a visual system around the insight that while AI models can produce infinite outcomes from a singular idea, it is how they’re trained and tuned that brings focus and organization to the potential chaos of the AI landscape.

The idea for our concept stemmed from AI acting as a catalyst — a multiplying force — that iterates and amplifies an original idea. Inspired initially by fractals and patterns that occur in nature, a singular 2D circle multiplies to form complex, organized 3D structures.

The outcome is a versatile visual language that captures watsonx’s core elements as a suite of unique states, each capable of transitioning seamlessly from 2D vector designs to intricate 3D visualizations.
Along with a broader suite of companion designs and visual mechanisms to explain the breadth and nuance of this new platform.

pages.title: Chase — US Open — Doug Hindson — Creative Director

blocks.markdown: # Chase — US Open

*Role:*  Art Director

*Studio:*  BUCK

*Client:*  Chase

Chase has a longstanding partnership with the US Open tennis tournament, and they came to BUCK looking for a spot that would celebrate this partnership, their financial tools, and the great city of New York.

Each scene was a love letter to the iconic sport of tennis, and iconic scenes from New York, where the tournament is held. From the brownstones of Queens, neighbourhood courts, and all the way to the Arthur Ashe stadium.

Inspired by the essential simplicity of the blue and green courts in the stadium, we kept the colour palette limited and shapes intentionally graphic and refined. We brought a sense of realism through rich lighting and dynamic camera angles — channeling the energy of the tournament itself.

pages.title: Dis\Connect — Doug Hindson — Creative Director

blocks.markdown: # Dis\Connect
*Role:*  Director, Designer, Writer, Fabricator

A search for higher meaning, dissatisfaction with the status quo and a sense that you’re the first person to feel this way. You're not. A semi-satirical coming of age story told by handmade wooden puppets.

## "This quiet, unassuming short with a truly excellent and funny script is tearjerkingly perfect."

[It’s Nice That](http://www.itsnicethat.com/articles/doug-hindson-disconnect)

‘DIS \ CONNECT’ was my graduation film from the Illustration & Animation course at Kingston University. All models and sets were hand-made from wood & card, hundreds of individual pieces were designed, cut, sanded, glued and painted. Rather than stop-motion, the film was shot live-action with strings and rods controlling the puppets and everything was captured in-camera.

Awarded a [Vimeo Staff Pick](https://vimeo.com/116533375).

pages.title: Apple TV+ — Here We Are — Doug Hindson — Creative Director

blocks.markdown: # Apple TV+ — Here We Are

*Role:*  Concept Design

*Studio:*  StudioAKA

*Client:*  Apple TV+

'HERE WE ARE: Notes For Living On Planet Earth', is based on the No. 1 New York Times Bestseller and 2017's No. 1 TIME Best Book of the Year by Oliver Jeffers and follows Finn; a precocious child who, on Earth Day, learns about the wonders of the planet from his parents — and from a mysterious exhibit at the aptly titled Museum of Everything.
I joined the project early on, helping to translate Oliver Jeffers’ beautiful hand-drawn line-work into expanded environments and props, that would then be recreated in 3D.

Although the approach used a lot of traditional mark making techniques, like pencil lines and brush strokes, the 3D models would be lit realistically — so the concept design needed to really emphasise the lighting and sense of space.

The original book had plenty of source material to draw from, however many of the scenes in the film were completely new and required a great deal of research. Looking for aspects from New York streets, brownstone apartments and aging museums, to plan layouts and understand what the camera would see from each angle.

Many of the original drawings simply wouldn’t have been able to exist in a fully dimensional space, so the challenge was to incorporate the charming wonkiness of of the line-work with layouts that would work in-camera. The end result being a blend of warm human details, and a natural sense of space and light.

pages.title: IBM — Partnerships — Doug Hindson — Creative Director

blocks.markdown: # IBM — Partnerships

*Role:*  Associate Creative Director, Art Direction, Design

*Studio:*  BUCK

*Client:*  IBM

BUCK was tasked with creating a wide array of imagery to accompany IBM’s messaging for each of their partnerships, across sport and entertainment. From graphic 2D vector illustrations and motion, to fully 3D representations — all designed to be used across a wide array of media and channels.

IBM brings its technologies, insights, and data expertise to every one of their partnerships. This sentiment was captured as ‘Partners in Progress’; a concept that brings IBM’s data-driven point of view together with specific themes and elements drawn from each of their partnerships, in a celebration of progress.

Part of the process was to distil everything into a set of conceptual and practical guidelines, enabling correct usage of the assets across many placements, and also to allow for future assets to be created cohesively.
## Fantasy Football

Modular, customizable, and overtly game-like. Fantasy Football visualizes the control, customization, and decision making central to every fantasy player’s experience.

Maybe more than any other partnership, data is a core part of that experience; Fantasy Football is fundamentally about data driving choices: Making changes, customizing your approach, reacting and adapting to new outcomes.
## The US Open

The US Open visuals strip away nearly all elements of the game, sharpening focus toward the iconic blue court of the US Open and the tennis ball itself.

Data becomes apparent through the trajectory of each stoke. Every shot, rally, game, set, and match is captured and can be visualized; overlaid and condensed in space and time into one sculptural moment. Balls travel on arcing threads of suspended data and we see instances of balls frozen in space at the point where they come into contact with an unseen racket.
## The Masters

Players performances are recorded in sequence through instances of clubs, balls, and flag pins. Strokes mapped as a network of paths over the course. Every shot putted toward a single hole in order.

These sequences create understandable timelines and and the impression of richly organized performance and statistical data, rooted in the environment and equipment of the sport.
## Wimbledon

Inspired by radial floral motifs, the sweeping arcs of racket strokes, and the overlapping photographic studies of Eadweard Muybridge, Wimbledon’s concept is centered around data drawn from the past and present, and the potential outcomes that data suggests.

Through overlapping sequential forms, snapshots of the past are captured and quantified, the present tracked, and potential predictions of future performance are made.
## The GRAMMYs

Motion, pattern, light, and drama. The GRAMMYs brings IBM’s design sensibilities to the stage, establishing an active and reactive array of graphic shape, light, and sound waves.

Taking the main stage as inspiration, we bringing a sense of performance, drama, glamor and excitement to data the data behind the event through highly choreographed light, pattern, and motion inspired by sound.
